source_question.stem: For the linear graph representing $2x + 3y = 12$, any two distinct points $P(x_1, y_1)$ and $Q(x_2, y_2)$ lie on the line. Which statement correctly explains why the ratio $\frac{y_2 - y_1}{x_2 - x_1}$ remains constant (invariant) regardless of which pair of points on the line is chosen?

options.label: A
options.text: Because the line passes through the origin $(0, 0)$.

options.label: B
options.text: Any two right-angled slope triangles constructed along the line are similar by AA similarity, making the ratio of vertical rise to horizontal run invariant.

options.label: C
options.text: Because the Euclidean distance between any two chosen points is always constant.

options.label: D
options.text: Because the sum of the coordinates $x + y$ is always equal to $12$.

answer.value: Any two right-angled slope triangles constructed along the line are similar by AA similarity, making the ratio of vertical rise to horizontal run invariant

hint_ladder.hint1_conceptual_nudge: Consider constructing right-angled triangles using horizontal run and vertical rise between pairs of points on the line.
hint_ladder.hint2_tactical_step: Examine the corresponding angles formed by the line with parallel horizontal grid lines to identify triangle similarity.

distractor_rationales.opt-A: Student assumes all lines pass through origin; here 2(0)+3(0)=0 != 12.
distractor_rationales.opt-C: Student confuses constant slope ratio with constant distance between points.
distractor_rationales.opt-D: Student confuses the linear relation 2x + 3y = 12 with simple coordinate sum x + y = 12.

core1a.title: Linear Graphs and Slope Invariance
core1a.concept: A straight line in the Cartesian plane has a constant inclination angle with the horizontal axis. Any two slope triangles have identical angle measures (AA similarity), forcing the ratio of vertical change to horizontal change to be invariant.
core1a.boundary_conditions: For vertical lines x = c, horizontal run is zero, making slope undefined.

core1b.prediction_prompt: If two right triangles share equal non-right angles, what is true about the ratio of their legs?
scaffold_steps: Formulate proportional ratio of corresponding sides

html_representation:
For the linear graph representing $2x + 3y = 12$, any two distinct points $P(x_1, y_1)$ and $Q(x_2, y_2)$ lie on the line. Which statement correctly explains why the ratio $\frac{y_2 - y_1}{x_2 - x_1}$ remains constant (invariant) regardless of which pair of points on the line is chosen?

Consider constructing right-angled triangles using horizontal run and vertical rise between pairs of points on the line.

Examine the corresponding angles formed by the line with parallel horizontal grid lines to identify triangle similarity.

Review Slope Invariance
Show Complete Solution

The line acts as a transversal across horizontal and vertical grid lines. For any two points, the horizontal run and vertical rise form a right-angled triangle.

Because the angle of inclination of the straight line is constant, all such slope triangles have congruent corresponding angles (AA similarity). Therefore, the ratio of legs $\frac{\Delta y}{\Delta x}$ is strictly invariant.
